cvBuilder.adviceSubtitle: Use these priorities to refine the draft. The advice is based on the information in your profile; it does not add or assume new achievements.

advice.targetMajor: Your intended major is {major}. Prioritize coursework, projects, or research that genuinely supports this field. For each selected item, state your exact contribution, the methods or tools you used, and a result that can be verified; keep the headline consistent with the program and do not add skills or outcomes that are not in your record.
advice.targetMajorMissing: Your profile does not name an intended major. Add the actual field or program before refining the headline; that will help you decide which coursework and projects belong near the top. Until you choose, keep the headline broad and factual rather than implying a specialization.
advice.evidence: The profile contains {count} project, research or recognition entries. Choose items that are relevant to the target application and that you can describe accurately; there is no universal number. For each, note your role, methods or tools, dates, and a verifiable outcome when available.
advice.evidenceMissing: No project, research or recognition evidence is recorded yet. Add relevant, verifiable work only if you have it; such entries are not required for every application. Do not invent activity to fill this gap.
advice.leadership: The profile lists {count} activity or leadership entries. Choose examples based on relevance and what they show about your interests, responsibilities, contribution and impact. Leadership is not universally preferred to other activities. Include dates or scale only when you can verify them.
advice.leadershipMissing: No activity or leadership role is recorded. Add real experiences only if they are relevant to your application; a formal title or leadership role is not universally required. Do not create one.
advice.academicComplete: Academic details are present in your profile. Verify every value and course name against official records. Include GPA, coursework or test results only when accurate and relevant to the target application; test requirements, waivers and alternatives vary.
advice.academicIncomplete: Some academic details are missing. Add GPA with its scale, graduation year or coursework only if the target programme requests it or you choose to share it. Use official school records; do not estimate or convert values.
advice.testScoresPresent: Test scores are listed. Verify them against the official report and check the target programme’s current requirements; exams, waivers and alternatives vary. Include only accurate, current results relevant to the application.
advice.testScoresMissing: No standardized test score is listed. Add an official result only if you took the exam and your target programme requests or accepts it. Requirements, waivers and alternatives vary; otherwise leave it out.
advice.lengthOnePage: This draft is estimated to fit on one page by a rough line count. Keep accurate, relevant information and follow the target institution’s current format and length instructions; there is no universal page rule.
advice.lengthLong: This draft is estimated at {pages} pages by a rough line count. Length expectations vary by country, institution, programme and application. Check target-specific instructions; remove repetition or unrelated details without making the text difficult to read.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.intro: A practical guide to using ScholarBridge for your study-abroad planning.

product.question: What does ScholarBridge help me do?
product.answer: ScholarBridge brings your study goals, university research, applications, documents and planning tools together. Recommendations depend on the information in your profile and are a starting point for your own research—not an admission or funding decision.

scores.question: Are fit scores or readiness percentages admission probabilities?
scores.answer: No. They summarize selected profile details or checklist progress. They are not probabilities, guarantees or an assessment by a university. Admissions decisions depend on each institution and applicant pool.

scholarship.question: How do I know if a scholarship is open to me?
scholarship.answer: Eligibility can depend on citizenship, degree level, course, financial need and the application cycle. Review the current official scholarship page before relying on a listing; contact the provider if an important condition is unclear.

costs.question: Can I rely on the costs and deadlines shown here?
costs.answer: Use them for planning, not as a substitute for an official fee schedule or application portal. Costs, exchange rates and deadlines can change; check the university or award provider's current source before making a payment or submitting an application.

gpaConversion.question: How do I convert an Uzbek 5-point or 100-point GPA to the 4.0 scale?
gpaConversion.answer: Enter your exact official GPA and select your original scale (5.0, 100, or 4.0) in your ScholarBridge profile. Our converter normalizes your score for eligibility comparisons while preserving your original scale on your CV and application records—never overwrite your official transcript grade with an unofficial self-conversion.

multiCurrency.question: How does the multi-currency Cost Calculator handle EUR, GBP, KRW, CAD, and UZS?
multiCurrency.answer: ScholarBridge converts published university tuition and living figures across 24 currencies (including USD, UZS, EUR, GBP, KRW, CAD, AUD, CHF, JPY, and SGD) and fills any unpublished insurance, books, flights from Tashkent, and visa fee lines using verified 2026 government benchmarks clearly badged as country benchmarks.

elYurtUmidi.question: How does the El-Yurt Umidi Foundation scholarship work for Uzbek students?
elYurtUmidi.answer: The El-Yurt Umidi Foundation under the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan funds Bachelor, Master, and PhD study abroad—covering tuition, living stipend, health insurance, and annual flights—for Uzbek citizens admitted to top-ranked global universities (especially QS/THE/ARWU Top 300) who commit to returning and contributing to Uzbekistan after graduation.

gksKorea.question: What is the difference between GKS Embassy Track and University Track in South Korea?
gksKorea.answer: Through the Embassy Track (Embassy of the Republic of Korea in Tashkent), you apply to 3 universities including at least one Type B regional university. Through the University Track, you apply directly to 1 Korean university (such as KAIST, POSTECH, UNIST, or SNU). GKS covers 100% tuition, round-trip airfare, a monthly stipend, and 1 year of Korean language training.

sperrkontoGermany.question: How much money is required in a German Blocked Account (Sperrkonto) for 2026–2027?
sperrkontoGermany.answer: For the 2026–2027 academic year, the German Embassy in Tashkent requires proof of €11,904 per year (€992 per month for 12 months) in an approved Sperrkonto (such as Expatrio or Fintiba), unless you hold a recognized full public scholarship like DAAD or El-Yurt Umidi.

sponsorAffidavit.question: What financial documents do my parents need to sponsor my student visa?
sponsorAffidavit.answer: Embassies require an official stamped bank balance statement in the sponsor’s name, a signed Affidavit or Letter of Financial Support, your translated birth certificate proving the parent-child relationship, and official annual income and tax payment certificates (which can be downloaded with a QR code via my.gov.uz / soliq.uz in Uzbekistan).

englishWaivers.question: Can I get an IELTS or TOEFL waiver if my Bachelor degree in Uzbekistan was taught in English?
englishWaivers.answer: Many graduate programs in Europe, the US, and the UK grant an English test waiver if you completed a full degree taught 100% in English at an accredited international university (such as WIUT, INHA University in Tashkent, Webster, or New Uzbekistan University) and submit an official Medium of Instruction (MOI) certificate. Always verify the specific program’s waiver rule first.

visaMockInterview.question: How should I prepare for my US F-1, UK Student Route, or German Embassy visa interview in Tashkent?
visaMockInterview.answer: Focus on four pillars: (1) why you selected your specific university and curriculum, (2) how your academic background prepared you, (3) exact knowledge of your annual Cost of Attendance, scholarship coverage, and sponsor income, and (4) your concrete career plan in Uzbekistan after graduation. Use our Visa Prep hub to practice country-specific checklists.

documentApostille.question: How and when do I get a Hague Apostille on my Uzbek diploma and transcripts?
documentApostille.answer: Destination countries such as South Korea, Germany, Italy, Hungary, Turkey, and Poland require a Hague Apostille on your original high school attestat or university diploma. In Uzbekistan, apply for an official e-Apostille through my.gov.uz or the Ministry of Justice / Ministry of Foreign Affairs before completing your notarized translation.

proPlanValue.question: What is free on ScholarBridge and what does Pro unlock?
proPlanValue.answer: University discovery, scholarship matching, multi-currency cost calculation, deadline tracking, task roadmaps, and reading the community forum are free. Pro unlocks unlimited AI Statement of Purpose and essay coaching, 24/7 AI Counselor deep reviews, Scholarship Autopilot drafting, and posting new threads in the community.

publicFeatures.heroTitle: You saw one grant. What does the site do next?
publicFeatures.heroBody: This is not just a list of announcements: the site picks grants that match your profile, explains the catalogue fit, tracks deadlines and helps with the paperwork. Browsing needs no account.
